note: Edge cases where query engines most often disagree. Every probe is deterministic: it orders its own output, aliases every projection, and avoids anything the SQL standard leaves open, unless `known_difference` records the divergence on purpose.

probes.sql: SELECT 3 AS probe WHERE 3 NOT IN (1, 2, NULL)
probes.why: Three-valued logic: `x NOT IN (1, 2, NULL)` can never be TRUE, so the row must be filtered out.

probes.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM probe_values WHERE v_int NOT IN (1, 2, NULL)
probes.why: Same three-valued rule applied to a column; any engine returning a count here is wrong.

probes.sql: SELECT SUM(v_int) AS s, COUNT(v_int) AS c, COUNT(*) AS n FROM probe_values WHERE FALSE
probes.why: SUM over an empty set is NULL while COUNT is 0.

probes.sql: SELECT (NULL = NULL) AS r
probes.why: Equality with NULL is unknown, not true.

probes.sql: SELECT (v_text || 'x') AS r FROM probe_values WHERE id = 4
probes.why: `||` propagates NULL.

probes.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT v_int) AS c FROM probe_values
probes.why: DISTINCT ignores NULLs.

probes.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM (SELECT DISTINCT g FROM probe_values) t
probes.why: DISTINCT collapses NULLs to a single group.

probes.sql: SELECT id FROM probe_values ORDER BY g ASC NULLS FIRST, id ASC LIMIT 3
probes.why: Explicit NULLS FIRST placement.

probes.sql: SELECT id FROM probe_values ORDER BY g DESC NULLS LAST, id ASC LIMIT 3
probes.why: Explicit NULLS LAST placement on a DESC key.

probes.sql: SELECT id FROM probe_values ORDER BY g ASC, id ASC LIMIT 3
probes.why: The implicit NULL placement must match the documented default.

probes.sql: SELECT v_int * 2 AS doubled FROM probe_values WHERE v_int IS NOT NULL ORDER BY doubled DESC, v_int ASC
probes.why: ORDER BY on a projection alias.

probes.sql: SELECT g, COUNT(*) AS n FROM probe_values GROUP BY g ORDER BY g NULLS FIRST
probes.why: NULL forms its own group.

probes.sql: SELECT 7 / 2 AS r
probes.known_difference: DuckDB's `/` always yields DOUBLE; DataFusion follows the standard's integer division. Compare manually.
probes.why: Kept in the catalogue as documentation of a deliberate dialect divergence.

probes.sql: SELECT (-7) % 3 AS r
probes.why: Sign of the remainder follows the dividend in the standard.

probes.sql: SELECT 7 % (-3) AS r
SELECT 0.1 + 0.2 AS r
SELECT CAST(2.5 AS INT) AS a, CAST(3.5 AS INT) AS b, CAST(-2.5 AS INT) AS c
probes.known_difference: Known upstream: #11886 'Float to int cast behaviour'. DataFusion truncates toward zero (2.5 -> 2, 1.999 -> 1) while the standard/PostgreSQL/DuckDB round half away from zero.

probes.sql: SELECT CAST('  12  ' AS INT) AS r
SELECT CAST('abc' AS INT) AS r
probes.why: Both engines should reject this; the probe is here to catch a silent 0 or NULL.

probes.sql: SELECT CAST('1e3' AS DOUBLE) AS r
SELECT CAST('2024-02-30' AS DATE) AS r
probes.why: 2024-02-30 does not exist; a silent wrap to 2024-03-01 would be a bug.

probes.sql: SELECT CAST(NULL AS INT) AS r
SELECT ROUND(2.5) AS a, ROUND(-2.5) AS b, ROUND(2.567, 2) AS c, ROUND(1.005, 2) AS d
probes.known_difference: Literal typing: DuckDB parses a bare `1.005` as DECIMAL and rounds exactly, DataFusion as DOUBLE where 1.005 is really 1.00499..., so ROUND gives 1.00. Not an arithmetic bug.

probes.sql: SELECT FLOOR(-2.5) AS f, CEIL(-2.5) AS c, TRUNC(-2.5) AS t

probes.why: Must raise an overflow error rather than wrap around in ANSI mode; in the default non-ANSI mode it is expected to wrap (see `integer_overflow_ansi`).
probes.known_difference: Not a bug: DataFusion defaults to `datafusion.execution.enable_ansi_mode=false`, where integer overflow wraps (Spark-compatible). The ANSI-side expectation is the separate probe `integer_overflow_ansi`, which now runs with `--session-option`; the gap it shows is tracked upstream by the epic #23929.

probes.sql: SELECT AVG(v_int) AS r FROM probe_values
SELECT STDDEV(v_int) AS s, STDDEV_POP(v_int) AS p FROM probe_values WHERE id = 1
SELECT STDDEV(v_int) AS s FROM probe_values WHERE v_int IS NULL
SELECT SUM(v_int) AS s FROM probe_values WHERE v_int IS NULL
SELECT MIN(v_text) AS lo, MAX(v_text) AS hi FROM probe_values WHERE v_text IS NOT NULL
SELECT g, SUM(v_int) AS s, AVG(v_dbl) AS a FROM probe_values GROUP BY g ORDER BY g NULLS FIRST
SELECT id, SUM(v_int) OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS s FROM probe_values ORDER BY g NULLS FIRST, id
SELECT id, SUM(v_int) OVER (ORDER BY v_int RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS s FROM probe_values WHERE v_int IS NOT NULL ORDER BY v_int, id
probes.why: RANGE includes peer rows with an equal ordering key, ROWS does not. The key is an integer so the probe tests frames, not float ordering.

probes.sql: SELECT id, SUM(v_int) OVER (ORDER BY v_int ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS s FROM probe_values WHERE v_int IS NOT NULL ORDER BY v_int, id
probes.why: RANGE includes peer rows with an equal ordering key, ROWS does not. The key is an integer so the probe tests frames, not float ordering.

probes.sql: SELECT id, LAG(v_int, 1, -1) OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY id) AS prev FROM probe_values ORDER BY g NULLS FIRST, id
SELECT id, NTILE(4) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS bucket FROM probe_values ORDER BY id

SELECT id, FIRST_VALUE(v_int) OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS f, LAST_VALUE(v_int) OVER (PARTITION BY g ORDER BY id ROWS BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS l FROM probe_values ORDER BY g NULLS FIRST, id
SELECT id, SUM(v_int) OVER (PARTITION BY g) AS s FROM probe_values ORDER BY g NULLS FIRST, id
probes.why: A NULL partition key still forms a partition.

probes.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM probe_values a LEFT JOIN probe_values b ON a.g = b.g WHERE a.g IS NULL
probes.why: NULL never matches NULL in a join predicate.

probes.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM probe_values a FULL OUTER JOIN probe_values b ON a.id = b.g
SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM probe_values a WHERE a.g IN (SELECT g FROM probe_values WHERE g IS NOT NULL)
SELECT LENGTH('héllo') AS a, LENGTH('日本語') AS b, LENGTH('') AS c
SELECT SUBSTRING('héllo', 2, 2) AS a, SUBSTRING('日本語', 2, 1) AS b
SELECT UPPER('ß') AS r
probes.why: Uppercasing ß is locale dependent; the result must at least be stable and documented.
probes.known_difference: Unicode full case folding (ß -> SS) in DataFusion versus simple case mapping (ß -> ẞ) in DuckDB. Both defensible; recorded so the daily hunt does not re-report it.

probes.sql: SELECT ('a' LIKE 'A') AS a, ('a' ILIKE 'A') AS b
SELECT TRIM('  x  ') AS a, LTRIM('  x  ') AS b, RTRIM('  x  ') AS c, TRIM(BOTH 'x' FROM 'xxaxx') AS d
SELECT REPLACE('abc', '', 'X') AS r
SELECT CONCAT('a', NULL) AS a, ('a' || NULL) AS b
SELECT GREATEST(NULL, 1) AS g, LEAST(NULL, 1) AS l
probes.why: Postgres ignores NULLs here; the standard leaves it open, so this probe mostly documents behaviour.

probes.sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', DATE '2024-03-15') AS r
SELECT DATE '2024-02-29' + INTERVAL '1' YEAR AS r
probes.why: Adding a year to a leap day has no obvious answer; behaviour must not be a silent panic.
probes.known_difference: Type divergence, low priority: DATE + INTERVAL yields DATE in DataFusion and TIMESTAMP in DuckDB/PostgreSQL. Surfaced here so it is not re-triaged as new.

probes.sql: SELECT DATE '2024-03-01' - DATE '2024-02-01' AS r
SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM DATE '2024-03-17') AS dow, EXTRACT(DOY FROM DATE '2024-03-17') AS doy
SELECT CAST('2024-03-15 12:34:56.789' AS TIMESTAMP) AS r
WITH s AS (SELECT g, COUNT(*) AS n FROM probe_values GROUP BY g) SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM s) AS groups, (SELECT SUM(n) FROM s) AS rows
probes.why: CTEs plus scalar subqueries must agree on row counts.

probes.sql: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT g FROM probe_values UNION ALL SELECT g FROM probe_values) t) AS all_rows, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT g FROM probe_values UNION SELECT g FROM probe_values) t) AS distinct_rows
SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN v_int IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS nulls, SUM(CASE v_int WHEN 4 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS fours FROM probe_values
SELECT COALESCE(NULL, NULL, 3) AS c, NULLIF(1, 1) AS n, NULLIF(1, 2) AS m
SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM probe_values WHERE v_int IN (1 + 1, 4)
SELECT x FROM (VALUES (0.0),(-0.0),(1.0)) AS t(x) ORDER BY x, 1
probes.known_difference: DataFusion sorts with the float total ordering, so -0.0 sorts before 0.0, while `=`, GROUP BY and DISTINCT treat them as equal (#24432 chose total ordering deliberately). DuckDB uses IEEE ordering. Documented, not a bug.
probes.why: Pins the total-ordering decision so a regression would be visible.

probes.sql: SELECT (-0.0 = 0.0) AS equal, COUNT(DISTINCT x) AS distinct_count FROM (VALUES (0.0),(-0.0)) AS t(x)
probes.why: Equality and DISTINCT use IEEE semantics even though ORDER BY uses total ordering.

probes.sql: SELECT map_extract(MAP {'a': 1, 'b': 2}, 'a') AS present, map_extract(MAP {'a': 1}, 'zz') AS missing
probes.why: DataFusion documents `map_extract` as returning a list, empty when the key is absent; DuckDB has the same function, so this is oracle-comparable.

probes.sql: SELECT element_at(MAP {'a': 1}, 'a') AS r
probes.known_difference: In DataFusion `element_at` is documented as an alias of `map_extract` (see information_schema.routines), while DuckDB's `element_at` is array access. Pinned so the divergence is not re-triaged as a bug; note that `element_at(<list>, i)` in DataFusion fails with a user-hostile error, recorded separately.
probes.why: Pins the documented alias so a change in either direction is visible.

probes.sql: SELECT CAST('1.10' AS DECIMAL(10,2)) * CAST('2.00' AS DECIMAL(10,2)) AS m, CAST('2.50' AS DECIMAL(4,2)) + CAST('0.05' AS DECIMAL(4,2)) AS a
probes.why: Decimal multiplication must widen the scale (2 + 2 = 4) rather than fall back to floating point, and decimal addition must stay exact -- 0.05 has no binary representation, so a silent promotion to DOUBLE shows up here.

probes.sql: SELECT CAST('1.00' AS DECIMAL(4,2)) / CAST('3.00' AS DECIMAL(4,2)) AS d
probes.why: Decimal division has no standardised result scale; the point of the probe is that DataFusion keeps a decimal result here and neither loses the type nor crashes.
probes.known_difference: Dialect divergence, not a bug: DataFusion keeps DECIMAL and applies its own result scale (scale 6 here -> 0.333333), while DuckDB promotes the result to DOUBLE (0.3333333333333333). DataFusion's decimal division rules are its own compatibility choice, tracked upstream as #7301 'Decimal division compatibility mode with spark'. Recorded so it is not re-triaged as a bug.

probes.sql: SELECT COALESCE(g, -1) AS g_key, COUNT(*) AS c FROM probe_values GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((g), ()) ORDER BY g_key, c
probes.why: GROUPING SETS must emit one row per grouping set, including the grand total over all 12 rows, and the NULL group must not be merged into it.

probes.sql: SELECT 0.1 + 0.2 AS r
probes.why: The first probe that exercises --session-option: with float literals parsed as DECIMAL the sum is exactly 0.3, which is also what DuckDB's DECIMAL literals give. It fails loudly if the option is ever silently ignored, which is the failure mode a session-option flag has.

Same expression as `integer_overflow`, with ANSI mode on: `enable_ansi_mode`'s own documentation promises that 'numeric overflow ... raise[s] runtime errors rather than returning NULL or adjusted values', so all three columns should be errors.
probes.known_difference: Known upstream: the ANSI mode epic #23929 names arithmetic overflow as in scope ('for example, invalid casts, arithmetic overflow, division by zero') and #24950 covers the spark-specific cast-overflow case. Measured 2026-10-15 on 55.2.0 with `enable_ansi_mode=true`: the three expressions still wrap to -9223372036854775808 / 9223372036854775807 / -2, i.e. the config documentation is ahead of the implementation. Recorded here so no slot re-files it as a new bug; revisit when #23929 lands.

probes.sql: SELECT COALESCE(g, -1) AS g_key, grouping(g) AS is_total, COUNT(*) AS c FROM probe_values GROUP BY ROLLUP(g) ORDER BY g_key, c
probes.why: ROLLUP must emit the same groups as the equivalent GROUPING SETS list, and `grouping(g)` must separate the NULL-valued group (`is_total = 0`, 2 rows) from the grand total (`is_total = 1`, all 12) -- the whole point of the flag, and the thing a plain COALESCE cannot tell apart.

probes.sql: SELECT id, SUM(v_int) OVER (ORDER BY v_int RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS s FROM probe_values ORDER BY id
probes.why: A RANGE frame is peer-based, not row-based: every row whose ORDER BY value ties must see the same running sum, and the NULL ordering value forms one peer group at the end. `probe_values` has ties (4,4 and 5,5) and NULLs precisely for this, and row-based `ROWS` semantics would give different numbers.

probes.sql: SELECT 'intersect_all' AS op, v FROM (SELECT v FROM (VALUES (1),(1),(1),(2)) t(v) INTERSECT ALL SELECT v FROM (VALUES (1),(1),(3)) u(v)) x UNION ALL SELECT 'except_all' AS op, v FROM (SELECT v FROM (VALUES (1),(1),(1),(2)) t(v) EXCEPT ALL SELECT v FROM (VALUES (1),(1),(3)) u(v)) y ORDER BY op, v
probes.why: The ALL variants of INTERSECT/EXCEPT are multiset operators with standard-fixed answers: with T1={1,1,1,2} (m copies) and T2={1,1,3} (n copies), INTERSECT ALL must emit min(m,n) copies of each row -- 1,1 -- and EXCEPT ALL must emit max(m-n,0) -- 1,2. One probe covers both operators because the same input pair drives both, and the `op` column keeps the two answers distinguishable.
probes.known_difference: Known upstream, already open -- not a new bug. DataFusion's ALL set operators do not implement multiset semantics. Measured 2026-10-15 on 55.2.0 (1 and 4 partitions identical, so it is not a planning artifact): INTERSECT ALL returns 1,1,1 (all three LHS copies) where the standard and DuckDB give 1,1; EXCEPT ALL returns only 2 where the standard and DuckDB give 1,2, i.e. it removes every LHS copy of a row that appears at all on the RHS. Filed upstream as apache/datafusion#12955 'INTERSECT ALL returns wrong number of records from RHS' and #12956 'EXCEPT ALL returns the wrong number of records' (both open since 2024-10-15, both quoting the same SQL-92 paragraph). Recorded here so no slot re-files it as new; revisit when either issue is fixed, and flip this probe to a pinned `expect_rows` at that point.

probes.sql: SELECT 'gs' AS src, value AS v FROM generate_series(1,5) AS g(value) UNION ALL SELECT 'range' AS src, value AS v FROM range(5,-1,-2) AS r(value) ORDER BY src, v
probes.why: First coverage of the TABLE function family: `information_schema.routines` lists exactly two functions with function_type='TABLE' (`generate_series`, `range`) and nothing -- neither a probe nor `df_robust.py --function-type` -- had ever exercised them. Covers both functions, ascending and descending steps in one query. `range` is end-exclusive, so `range(5,-1,-2)` must stop before -1 and yield 5,3,1 (a difference in end-exclusivity or step direction is visible in the pinned rows).

probes.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS c, MIN(v) AS lo, MAX(v) AS hi FROM generate_series(1, 9223372036854775806, 9223372036854775805) AS g(v)
probes.why: The series generator has to advance with a checked add: the naive `current + step` overflows i64 here (1 + i64::MAX-ish), and an overflow in a `next` computation is a PANIC-class regression, not a wrong answer. The correct series is [1, 9223372036854775806], i.e. exactly two rows, so the probe is bounded and safe to run every slot. Verified 2026-10-16 on 55.2.0: no panic, no wrap.

probes.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS c, MIN(CAST(v AS DATE)) AS lo, MAX(CAST(v AS DATE)) AS hi FROM generate_series(DATE '2024-01-01', DATE '2024-01-03', INTERVAL '1' DAY) AS g(v)
probes.why: The third argument of `generate_series` is an interval when the bounds are DATE/TIMESTAMP, a different code path from the integer form; the endpoints are asserted as DATEs so the pinned answer is free of timestamp-rendering differences between the engines. Three days inclusive must give three rows.
